title: Non-braid-like Reidemeister moves are generated by braid-like moves and reducing moves
statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every non-braid-like Reidemeister move of type II acting on one Seifert circle, and every non-braid-like Reidemeister move of type III, is a composition of Reidemeister I moves, braid-like Reidemeister II and III moves, Yamada-Vogel reducing moves, and their inverses. Hence any two diagrams of the same link can be connected by a sequence of moves of the four types I, braid-like II, braid-like III and reducing (and inverses).
strategy: Case analysis as in Traczyk's Lemma 4 and Figure 3: a non-braid-like R3 is replaced by a non-braid-like R2, a diagram isotopy, a braid-like R3 and another non-braid-like R2 (one local picture is drawn; the remaining orientation and sign variants are obtained by reflecting the picture and reversing orientations). A non-braid-like R2 on two arcs of the same Seifert circle is replaced by two R1 moves (creating two new Seifert circles) followed by a reducing move and its inverse; when the two arcs lie on distinct Seifert circles the move is already a reducing move up to orientation. Every move of type I is braid-like by definition, which gives the stated generating set. The case analysis works with reducing moves and defect regions, so AC is inherited through the annulus lemma used to define coherence and the height function.

references.title: Traczyk, A new proof of Markov's braid theorem, Banach Center Publications 42 (1998), 409-419
Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
